children: Kazakhstan plans to issue five-year sovereign Eurobonds across three trading venues, according to a statement released on Wednesday by Teniz Capital, the Kazakh lead manager for the deal.

The issuance is planned for the London Stock Exchange, the Kazakhstan Stock Exchange, and the Astana International Exchange, "depending on favourable market conditions", it said. It did not say what the bonds' volume would be.
Citi, JPMorgan and Société Générale are acting as joint lead managers and bookrunners, it said.

Kazakhstan has been borrowing funds for several consecutive years to refinance debt and cover its budget deficit amid low energy and metal prices. The deficit is projected to reach 4.6 trillion tenge ($10.3 billion) in 2026.
